# InkOS — Base UI error #31 hotfix

## Context

Production is broken on every authenticated page after commit `200eb35` (the sidebar bug-fix sprint merged as PR #6 into `main`). The browser throws:

```
Error: Base UI error #31
    at i_ (.../0qosc3o6d2baw.js:24:110648)
    at oq (...145743)
    at su (...185747)
```

The error fires during React render/hydration on every authenticated route.

## Root cause

Base UI error code 31 comes from `node_modules/@base-ui/react/menu/group/MenuGroupContext.js` line 17:

```js
throw new Error('Base UI: MenuGroupRootContext is missing. Menu group parts must be used within <Menu.Group>.');
```

The error fires when `MenuPrimitive.GroupLabel` mounts without a surrounding `MenuPrimitive.Group`. Our `components/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx` maps `DropdownMenuLabel` onto `MenuPrimitive.GroupLabel`, so any `<DropdownMenuLabel>` used without an enclosing `<DropdownMenuGroup>` throws.

### Why it's only showing up now

The `DropdownMenuLabel` pattern without a surrounding Group has existed for a while in AppHeader, StudioSwitcher, LocationSwitcher (all latent error #31 triggers). But the newly-shipped dropdowns push one of them onto the render path of every page load — the SidebarUserFooter dropdown from commit `200eb35` is rendered on every authenticated route, and Base UI's dropdown primitives appear to be instantiating context during mount, tripping the error even before the dropdown is clicked.

## Affected files (5 call sites of `DropdownMenuLabel`)

Every file uses `DropdownMenuLabel` directly under `DropdownMenuContent`, with no `DropdownMenuGroup` wrapper:

| File | Line | Current usage |
|---|---|---|
| `components/app/sidebar/SidebarUserFooter.tsx` | ~125 | Profile header (avatar + name + email + role) |
| `components/app/sidebar/AppHeader.tsx` | ~358 | Top-right user menu header |
| `components/shared/StudioSwitcher.tsx` | ~130 | "Switch studio" heading |
| `components/shared/LocationSwitcher.tsx` | ~88 | "Switch location" heading |
| `components/messages/Composer.tsx` | ~234 | "Quick templates" heading |

None of the 5 uses `DropdownMenuGroup` around the label.

## Recommended fix — one-line wrapper change

Modify the primitive wrapper `components/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx` so that `DropdownMenuLabel` internally wraps its child `MenuPrimitive.GroupLabel` inside a `MenuPrimitive.Group`. This fixes ALL 5 call sites without touching any of them.

### Exact diff

**File:** `components/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx` (lines ~56–74)

```ts
// BEFORE
function DropdownMenuLabel({
  className,
  inset,
  ...props
}: MenuPrimitive.GroupLabel.Props & { inset?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <MenuPrimitive.GroupLabel
      data-slot="dropdown-menu-label"
      data-inset={inset}
      className={cn(
        "px-1.5 py-1 text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground data-inset:pl-7",
        className
      )}
      {...props}
    />
  )
}

// AFTER
function DropdownMenuLabel({
  className,
  inset,
  ...props
}: MenuPrimitive.GroupLabel.Props & { inset?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <MenuPrimitive.Group>
      <MenuPrimitive.GroupLabel
        data-slot="dropdown-menu-label"
        data-inset={inset}
        className={cn(
          "px-1.5 py-1 text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground data-inset:pl-7",
          className
        )}
        {...props}
      />
    </MenuPrimitive.Group>
  )
}
```

### Why this over the alternative

Alternative would be to wrap `<DropdownMenuLabel>` in `<DropdownMenuGroup>` in each of the 5 caller files. The alternative is more ARIA-correct (a group should contain the label plus its related items), but:

- 5× blast radius vs. 1-file change
- The 5 current uses treat the label as a visual heading, not a semantic group label — none of them actually have related sub-items that a screen-reader group would benefit from
- The wrapper fix keeps future usages safe without every new caller having to remember the rule
- Visual layout unaffected: `MenuPrimitive.Group` renders a bare `<div role="group">` with no padding/margin

ARIA cost is minor: each label sits inside a group with no siblings, which is equivalent to an empty landmark. Not a regression vs. the current behavior (which is just a loose label inside the menu popup).

## Verification

Before committing:

1. **Typecheck clean** — `pnpm typecheck`
2. **Build clean** — `pnpm build`
3. **Local dev smoke** — `pnpm dev`, open any authenticated page (`/today`, `/clients`, `/projects`), confirm:
   - No "Base UI error #31" in browser console
   - No error boundary rendered
   - Sidebar profile dropdown opens on click and shows header + items
   - AppHeader top-right user menu opens and shows header + items
   - Studio switcher in AppHeader opens (if multi-studio available)
   - Messages composer template picker opens and shows "Quick templates" heading

After deploying to main:

- Navigate to `https://inkos.up.railway.app/today` in an incognito window
- No error on page load
- Click the bottom-of-sidebar profile — dropdown opens cleanly
- Click through every menu item

## Critical files

- **Modify:** `components/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx` (one function, ~6 lines added)

That's it. No other file changes needed.

## Out of scope (not touching this sprint)

- Refactoring the 5 caller files to use proper `DropdownMenuGroup` semantics — can ship that as a polish PR later if ARIA audit needs it
- The earlier Explore agent's theory that "render + children" on `DropdownMenuTrigger` is the cause — confirmed FALSE after reading base-ui source (error #31 is specifically the GroupLabel/Group context error, not composition). That pattern is correct.

1	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
2	import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
3	import { createClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server'
4	import { TodayClient } from '@/components/today/TodayClient'
5	import { ArtistTodayDashboard } from '@/components/today/ArtistTodayDashboard'
6	import type { GettingStartedCounts } from '@/components/dashboard/GettingStartedCard'
7	import { getArtistIdForUser, getArtistEarningsToday } from '@/lib/today/queries'
8	import type { Database } from '@/lib/supabase/types'
9	
10	export const metadata: Metadata = {
11	  title: 'Today — InkOS',
12	}
13	
14	type StudioRole = Database['public']['Tables']['studio_members']['Row']['role']
15	
16	export default async function TodayPage() {
17	  const supabase = await createClient()
18	  const {
19	    data: { user },
20	  } = await supabase.auth.getUser()
21	
22	  if (!user) redirect('/login')
23	
24	  const [profileResult, memberResult] = await Promise.all([
25	    supabase
26	      .from('profiles')
27	      .select('full_name')
28	      .eq('id', user.id)
29	      .single(),
30	    supabase
31	      .from('studio_members')
32	      .select('studio_id, role, studios(name)')
33	      .eq('user_id', user.id)
34	      .is('deactivated_at', null)
35	      .order('created_at', { ascending: true })
36	      .limit(1)
37	      .single(),
38	  ])
39	
40	  const firstName = profileResult.data?.full_name?.split(' ')[0] ?? 'there'
41	  const studioName =
42	    (memberResult.data?.studios as { name: string } | null)?.name ?? 'My Studio'
43	  const hasStudio = !!memberResult.data?.studio_id
44	  const studioId = memberResult.data?.studio_id
45	  const role: StudioRole = memberResult.data?.role ?? 'owner'
46	
47	  let gettingStartedCounts: GettingStartedCounts = {
48	    services: 0,
49	    artists: 0,
50	    schedules: 0,
51	    bookings: 0,
52	    bookingPageConfigured: false,
53	  }
54	
55	  let ownArtistId: string | null = null
56	  let artistEarningsToday = 0
57	
58	  if (studioId) {
59	    const [servicesRes, artistsRes, schedulesRes, bookingsRes, bpRes] = await Promise.all([
60	      supabase
61	        .from('services')
62	        .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
63	        .eq('studio_id', studioId),
64	      supabase
65	        .from('artists')
66	        .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
67	        .eq('studio_id', studioId),
68	      supabase
69	        .from('artist_schedules')
70	        .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
71	        .eq('studio_id', studioId),
72	      supabase
73	        .from('bookings')
74	        .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
75	        .eq('studio_id', studioId),
76	      supabase
77	        .from('booking_page_settings')
78	        .select('studio_id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
79	        .eq('studio_id', studioId),
80	    ])
81	
82	    gettingStartedCounts = {
83	      services: servicesRes.count ?? 0,
84	      artists: artistsRes.count ?? 0,
85	      schedules: schedulesRes.count ?? 0,
86	      bookings: bookingsRes.count ?? 0,
87	      bookingPageConfigured: (bpRes.count ?? 0) > 0,
88	    }
89	
90	    if (role === 'artist' || role === 'guest_artist') {
91	      ownArtistId = await getArtistIdForUser(supabase, studioId, user.id)
92	      if (ownArtistId) {
93	        artistEarningsToday = await getArtistEarningsToday(supabase, studioId, ownArtistId)
94	      }
95	    }
96	  }
97	
98	  // S19: artist and guest_artist roles see their personal artist dashboard
99	  if ((role === 'artist' || role === 'guest_artist') && studioId && ownArtistId) {
100	    return (
101	      <ArtistTodayDashboard
102	        firstName={firstName}
103	        studioId={studioId}
104	        artistId={ownArtistId}
105	        artistEarningsToday={artistEarningsToday}
106	      />
107	    )
108	  }
109	
110	  return (
111	    <TodayClient
112	      firstName={firstName}
113	      studioName={studioName}
114	      hasStudio={hasStudio}
115	      studioId={studioId ?? null}
116	      role={role}
117	      ownArtistId={ownArtistId}
118	      artistEarningsToday={artistEarningsToday}
119	      gettingStartedCounts={gettingStartedCounts}
120	    />
121	  )
122	}

Excellent. Now I have enough information to provide a comprehensive audit. Let me compile the report:

## InkOS Server-Side Performance Audit

### CRITICAL FINDINGS (Biggest Waterfalls)

**1. App Layout — Sequential Studio Resolution Bottleneck (≈150ms estimated latency)**

File: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS/app/(app)/layout.tsx`

The layout executes **10+ queries sequentially in two phases**:
- **Phase 1 (Sequential):** `getUser()` → `getActiveStudio()` → `getActiveLocation()`
  - `getActiveStudio()` itself does 2-3 queries: `auth.getUser()`, `studio_members.select()` (joins `studios`), then a Promise.all loop querying `subscriptions` once per studio (N+1 pattern for multi-studio users)
  - `getActiveLocation()` queries `locations` for the studio
  - These are **strictly sequential** (line 44 awaits location after studio completes)
  - **Estimated latency: 100–150ms** at 50ms per query

- **Phase 2 (Parallelized):** 8 badge queries + artist lookup (Promise.all, lines 67–128)
  - Then a second Promise.all for pins + MTD commissions (line 132)
  - **If parallelized correctly, this is ~100ms**, but artists take an extra sequential query first (lines 57–65)

**Waterfall estimate for slowest path (artist role, multi-studio):** 200–250ms just to render the sidebar.

---

**2. Inbox Page — N+1 in Assignment Mapping (≈70ms extra latency)**

File: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS/app/(app)/inbox/page.tsx`

- 7 queries in Promise.all (good parallelization, lines 43–73)
- **BUT:** The assignment fetch (line 57) returns ALL assignments for the studio (`no .limit()`), then client-side loops build a Map (line 79–86)
  - For studios with thousands of inbox assignments, this pulls massive result set unnecessarily
  - **Missing: `.limit()` or proper filtering** to active/unresolved items only

- Item normalization loops are wasteful (lines 93–161) — multiple type checks per item, no memoization
- **Impact:** Inbox with 1000+ archived assignments slows by 50–100ms

---

### TABLE 1: Top-Traffic Pages Query Inventory

| Page | Total Queries | In Promise.all | Sequential Awaits | Wildcard Select | Missing Limits | Est. Latency |
|------|---------------|----------------|-------------------|-----------------|----------------|--------------|
| **dashboard** | 5 + 3 (artist) | 5 | 1 (artist lookup) | None | None (all count) | 100–150ms |
| **inbox** | 7 | 7 | None | None | 1 (assignments) | 120–160ms |
| **calendar** | Client-side (CalendarPageClient) | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | Deferred |
| **clients** | 2 | 2 | None | **YES** (35 cols) | None (limit 50) | 80–120ms |
| **payments** | 0 (layout-deferred) | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | Lazy-loaded |
| **projects** | 2 | 2 | None | None | None (limit 100) | 80–120ms |
| **messages** | 4–5 | 2 (list + conversation) | 1 (messages + bookings) | None | None (limit 50) | 120–160ms |

---

### HIGH-IMPACT EASY WINS

**1. Clients Page Wildcard Select (15–20% speedup, 1 line)**

**Current (line 29):**
```typescript
.select('id, studio_id, first_name, last_name, ... [35 cols total]')
```

**Issue:** Fetches every column including notes, address, pronouns, avatar_url, etc. Most aren't rendered in the list view.

**Recommendation:** Scope to ~12 essential columns for the list, defer detail columns to detail page:
```typescript
.select('id, first_name, last_name, email, phone, total_spent_cents, last_visit_at, created_at, archived_at')
```

**Estimated saving:** 20–30ms per page load.

---

**2. Inbox Assignment Query — Add Missing `.limit()`**

**Current (line 57):**
```typescript
.from('inbox_assignments')
.select('item_kind, item_id, assigned_to, snoozed_until, archived_at, resolved_at')
.eq('studio_id', studioId)  // ← No limit, fetches ALL
```

**Fix:**
```typescript
.select(...)
.eq('studio_id', studioId)
.or('(archived_at.is.null,snoozed_until.gt.now())') // Only active items
.limit(500)
```

**Estimated saving:** 30–50ms for studios with 1000+ archived assignments.

---

**3. Projects Page N+1 Session Count (20–30% speedup)**

**Current (`lib/projects/queries.ts`, lines 113–130):**
```typescript
// Count completed sessions per project via separate query for each project
if (projectIds.length > 0) {
  const { data: sessionsData } = await supabase
    .from('bookings')
    .select('project_id, status')
    .in('project_id', projectIds)  // ← Correct, uses IN
    .eq('status', 'completed')
    .eq('studio_id', studioId)
}
```

This is **actually good** — uses `in()` not a loop. No N+1 here.

---

### MEDIUM-IMPACT OPTIMIZATIONS

**4. Active Studio Resolution (Extract into Cached Helper)**

**Current issue:** `getActiveStudio()` does an implicit N+1 when a user has 2+ studios:
```typescript
const membershipsWithPlan = await Promise.all(
  rows.map(async (row) => {
    const { data: sub } = await supabase
      .from('subscriptions')
      .select('plan_tier')
      .eq('studio_id', row.studio_id)  // ← Per-studio query
      .eq('status', 'active')
      .maybeSingle()
  })
)
```

**Fix:** Batch subscriptions into one query:
```typescript
if (rows.length > 0) {
  const studioIds = rows.map(r => r.studio_id)
  const { data: subs } = await supabase
    .from('subscriptions')
    .select('studio_id, plan_tier')
    .in('studio_id', studioIds)
    .eq('status', 'active')
  const subMap = new Map(subs.map(s => [s.studio_id, s]))
  // Then map using subMap instead of individual queries
}
```

**Estimated saving:** 100–150ms for users with 5+ studios (currently executing 5 queries serially).

---

**5. Layout → Active Location Sequential Dependency**

**Current (line 44):**
```typescript
const activeLocation = await getActiveLocation(studioId, role)  // After getActiveStudio()
```

**Could parallelize:** `getActiveLocation()` only needs `studioId` + `role`, both resolved after `getActiveStudio()`. Move both to the same Promise.all:

10. **React Query usage** — does the app have a single QueryClientProvider at the root? Is its default `staleTime` 0 (fetches on every mount) or set to something reasonable?

11. **`useEffect` mount-fetches** — client components that `useEffect(() => { fetch('/api/...') }, [])` on mount. Each one = extra round-trip AFTER the page renders. Find the heavy offenders.

12. **Realtime subscriptions on mount** — `hooks/use-realtime-messages.ts` was recently added. Are multiple subscriptions mounting simultaneously?

13. **Sentry SDK bundle size** — `instrumentation-client.ts` + `instrumentation.ts` — Sentry alone can be 100KB+ if not trimmed.

14. **`useQueryClient`, `useSearchParams`, `usePathname` usage frequency** — if every client component uses these, they cause unnecessary re-renders on route change.

Report in ≤700 words:
- Heaviest client-shipped code paths (file + approx bundle impact)
- Worst offenders for main-thread blocking
- Easy wins (wrap X in `dynamic()`, move Y to server, etc.)
- Fonts + images findings
- Any config issues in `next.config.ts`
- Recommended "first wins" list ranked by impact/effort

Also check `next.config.ts` settings that affect perf:
- `experimental.turbo` / turbopack flags
- `optimizePackageImports` 
- `compress`
- Image `domains` / `remotePatterns`

content.text: Based on my comprehensive audit, here is the performance analysis: --- ## InkOS Next.js 16 + React 19 Client-Side Bundle + Render Performance Audit ### Key Findings Summary **Overall Assessment:** The app has significant bundle bloat on authenticated routes due to heavy library payloads shipped client-side without adequate tree-shaking or lazy-loading. The realtime subscriptions hook is well-designed but the broader client component strategy needs refinement. --- ### 1. 'Use Client' Boundaries & Architecture **Status:** PROBLEMATIC - **38 `'use client'` files** under `/app/` (out of 168 .tsx files = 23%) - **355 `'use client'` files** under `/components/` — extremely high (nearly all interactive components are client-side) - **No pure RSC pages:** 0 of 79 top-level pages are pure RSC; all authenticated pages mount a client wrapper (`CalendarPageClient`, `ClientsPageClient`, `AppointmentsPageClient`, etc.) - **Impact:** Every page click routes through React hydration → full client JS bundle sent on initial load **Worst offenders:** - `/app/(app)/clients/ClientsPageClient.tsx` — mounts 3+ `useState` hooks, 81+ `useEffect` calls across 355 child components - `/app/(app)/calendar/_components/CalendarPageClient.tsx` — uses FullCalendar (heavy tree), `useRouter`, `useSearchParams`, `useMutation` - `/app/(app)/appointments/` — tabbed interface with full React Query integration --- ### 2. Heavy Dependencies Shipped Client-Side **Package.json analysis:** - `@fullcalendar/*` (6 pkgs, ~250KB gzipped) — used in `/components/calendar/CalendarView.tsx` — **NOT dynamically imported** - `recharts` (~180KB gzipped) — used in `/components/admin/billing/MrrDashboard.tsx` — **IS dynamically imported** (good) - `@tiptap/*` (3 pkgs, ~120KB gzipped) — used in `/components/clients/notes/AddNoteModal.tsx` — **IS dynamically imported via `dynamic()`** (good) - `date-fns` (~40KB gzipped) — 16 imports across app + components, all tree-shakeable but bundled on every route - `qrcode` (~20KB) — used only in `/components/settings/QrCodeCard.tsx` — not lazy-loaded - `react-hook-form` (~9KB) — used in form pages - `lucide-react` (282 imports in components!) — tree-shakeable but **could benefit from explicit subpath imports** - `twilio` (server-only, ~500KB) — **NOT in `serverExternalPackages`** — likely leaking to client bundle **Missing `serverExternalPackages` in next.config.ts:** The config file does **NOT** include: ```typescript serverExternalPackages: ['twilio', '@sentry/nextjs', ...], ``` This means Twilio could be bundled on clients that import from pages using it. --- ### 3. Dynamic Imports (Lazy-Loading) **Current lazy-loaded heavyweights (GOOD):** - `AddNoteModal` (Tiptap) — `/app/(app)/clients/ClientsPageClient.tsx` - `CalendarView` (FullCalendar) — `/app/(app)/calendar/_components/CalendarPageClient.tsx` — with `ssr: false` - `RechartsAreaChart`, `RechartsBarChart` — `/components/admin/AdminDashboardClient.tsx`, reports - `SchedulesPage` — `/app/(app)/artists/SchedulesTabClient.tsx` **NOT lazy-loaded (PROBLEM):** - **FullCalendar in `/components/calendar/CalendarView.tsx`** — imports 5 FullCalendar modules unconditionally at top of file despite being a `'use client'` component - **QRCode in `/components/settings/QrCodeCard.tsx`** — no dynamic import (small impact, ~20KB) - **@tiptap imports in client components** — Tiptap editor is only needed when modal opens, but imported statically **Missing opportunities (4 dynamic calls found):** - Many admin/reports pages could lazy-load recharts variants per view --- ### 4. Tree-Shaking Analysis **Lucide-React (282 imports across codebase):** - **Good pattern found:** `import { Plus, Loader2, AlertCircle } from 'lucide-react'` (named imports = tree-shakeable) - **No barrel imports detected** (no `import * as Icons`) - **Tree-shaking: EFFECTIVE** — Turbopack/Next 16 should remove unused icons **Date-fns (16 files, mostly tree-shakeable):** - All imports use named syntax: `import { format, parseISO } from 'date-fns'` — **GOOD** - No `import df from 'date-fns'` found - **Tree-shaking: EFFECTIVE** **React Query:** - Imported modularly across app (`useQuery`, `useMutation`, `useQueryClient`) - **Tree-shaking: EFFECTIVE** --- ### 5. Unoptimized Images **Count:** - **1 `` tag in `/app/`** (unoptimized) - **4 `` tags in `/components/`** (unoptimized) - **Total: 5 unoptimized images** **Offending files:** - Likely in avatar/logo components; should use `next/image` for LQIP, responsive srcsets --- ### 6. Fonts **Layout.tsx uses 3 Google fonts:** ```typescript const inter = Inter({ subsets: ['latin'], weight: ['400', '500', '600', '700', '800'] }) // 5 weights const instrumentSerif = Instrument_Serif({ subsets: ['latin'], weight: ['400'], style: ['normal', 'italic'] }) // 2 variants const jetbrainsMono = JetBrains_Mono({ subsets: ['latin'] }) // all weights ``` **Impact:** 8+ separate font requests + CSS injection **Optimization opportunity:** Remove unused weights (keep 400, 600, 700 for Inter; drop 500, 800) --- ### 7. Global CSS Size **`/app/globals.css`: 2,049 lines** This is above the 1500-line threshold for performance concerns. Likely contains: - Tailwind base layers - Custom utility classes for FullCalendar, Tiptap, etc. - Calendar color classes (`artist-event-1` through `artist-event-10`) --- ### 8. QueryClient Configuration **File:** `/lib/query-client.ts` **Config:** ```typescript staleTime: 60_000, // 60s fresh window — GOOD retry: 1, // vs default 3 — GOOD refetchOnWindowFocus: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' // dev-friendly ``` **Assessment:** **GOOD** — prevents redundant fetches. No aggressive re-fetching on mount. **QueryProvider wrapper:** Is a `'use client'` component (expected) and correctly placed at root level. --- ### 9. Mount-Time `useEffect` Data Fetches **Found 81 `useEffect` hooks across `/components/`** **Hot spots:** - `/app/(app)/clients/ClientsPageClient.tsx` — 3 major useEffects: - Load saved views on mount - Restore page from URL - Sync filter state - `/app/(app)/calendar/_components/CalendarPageClient.tsx` — multiple filter/date sync useEffects - `/app/(app)/artists/ArtistDetailClient.tsx` — fetch artist on mount - `/app/(app)/appointments/new/AppointmentWizardClient.tsx` — pre-load wizard state **Impact:** Each useEffect may trigger a network round-trip **AFTER** page renders, causing layout shift + slow paint --- ### 10. Realtime Subscriptions **File:** `/hooks/use-realtime-messages.ts` **Assessment:** **WELL-DESIGNED** - Two hooks: `useRealtimeMessages` + `useRealtimeConversationList` - Uses stable callback refs to prevent re-subscription - Only subscribes if IDs are present (no wasteful empty channels) - Cleans up subscriptions on unmount **No massive simultaneous subscriptions detected.** Usage appears scoped to Messages feature only. --- ### 11. Sentry SDK Bundle Impact **Files:** - `instrumentation.ts` (server) — lazy-loads Sentry config - `instrumentation-client.ts` (client) — imports `./sentry.client.config` - **Sentry @10.49.0** — likely 80–120KB gzipped in client bundle **Assessment:** Sentry is configured but impact unclear without bundle analysis. ClientCode should run `ANALYZE=true npm run build` to measure exact contribution. --- ### 12. `useSearchParams` / `usePathname` Usage **45 files in `/components/`** use these hooks **Impact:** These cause full component re-renders on navigation. Heavy use could cause jank. **Examples:** - `ClientsPageClient` uses `useSearchParams()` to restore filters - `CalendarPageClient` uses both hooks extensively --- ### Config Issues in `next.config.ts` 1. **Missing `serverExternalPackages`** — Should include: ```typescript serverExternalPackages: ['twilio', ...], ``` 2. **No `optimizePackageImports`** — Should add: ```typescript experimental: { optimizePackageImports: ['date-fns', 'lucide-react', ...], } ``` 3. **Turbopack enabled** (`turbopack: { root: __dirname }`) — Good, but not enough without package optimizations 4. **`output: 'standalone'`** — Good for Docker, but increases bundle analysis complexity --- ## Quick Wins Ranked by Impact/Effort | Rank | Action | Impact | Effort | Est. Savings | |------|--------|--------|--------|--------------| | 1 | Add `serverExternalPackages: ['twilio']` to next.config.ts | HIGH | TRIVIAL | 500KB* | | 2 | Lazy-load FullCalendar in CalendarView (wrap in dynamic()) | HIGH | LOW | 250KB | | 3 | Add `optimizePackageImports: ['date-fns', 'lucide-react']` | MEDIUM | LOW | 30–50KB | | 4 | Reduce Inter font weights (keep 400, 600, 700 only) | MEDIUM | TRIVIAL | 15–20KB | | 5 | Move 3 useEffects in ClientsPageClient to server via RSC + revalidation | MEDIUM | MEDIUM | 40KB | | 6 | Replace 5 `` with `next/image` for LQIP | LOW | LOW | 10KB + UX gain | | 7 | Split globals.css into per-route CSS modules | LOW | HIGH | 100KB* | | 8 | Audit Sentry client config for tree-shaking | MEDIUM | MEDIUM | 40–80KB | *Server-side savings only; frontend not directly reduced but reduces JS parse time. --- ## Verdict **Slowness root causes:** 1. **Near-zero RSC usage** — every page is full React client component 2. **FullCalendar not lazy-loaded** — 250KB on /calendar click 3. **No `serverExternalPackages`** — potential Twilio leak 4. **81 mount-time useEffects** — data fetches after render, causing jank **Next steps:** Run `ANALYZE=true npm run build` to measure actual bundle sizes per route, then prioritize #1 (serverExternalPackages) and #2 (FullCalendar lazy load).
Synthesizing the 3 audits into a prioritized plan.

input.content: # InkOS — Performance optimization sprint ## Context User reports every page click feels slow. Goal: make navigation feel instant. Three parallel Explore agents audited navigation/loading, server-side queries, and client-side bundle. Their combined findings point to one big perception problem and two real latency problems: 1. **No `loading.tsx` anywhere** → every click shows stale UI for 300–800 ms until the new page's Server Component finishes. User sees a blank delay; "it feels broken." 2. **Layout awaits 10+ Supabase queries on every navigation** → that's the real latency floor, roughly 200–300 ms even with parallelization. 3. **Client bundle includes server-only code (Twilio) + heavyweight FullCalendar not properly split** → first paint + calendar page take a bundle hit. Fixing all three is ~600–900 ms of perceived + real latency reduction per click, plus 300–500 KB off the wire for the Calendar page. The single biggest win — adding `loading.tsx` everywhere — takes less than an hour and makes every click feel instant even without touching the data path. ## Sprint plan — 4 sequenced sprints, shipped as ONE PR ### Sprint A — Instant click feel (biggest perceived win, ~45 min) **Goal:** Every click shows a branded skeleton within 100 ms of sidebar activation, regardless of how long the Server Component actually takes to finish. **New loading.tsx files to create:** - `app/(app)/dashboard/loading.tsx` — dashboard skeleton (KPI cards + queue + agenda) - `app/(app)/inbox/loading.tsx` — inbox list skeleton + tab bar - `app/(app)/calendar/loading.tsx` — calendar grid skeleton with header toolbar - `app/(app)/clients/loading.tsx` — table skeleton with filter row - `app/(app)/artists/loading.tsx` — team roster skeleton - `app/(app)/payments/loading.tsx` — tabs + table skeleton - `app/(app)/appointments/loading.tsx` — list + tabs skeleton - `app/(app)/projects/loading.tsx` — card-grid skeleton - `app/(app)/messages/loading.tsx` — two-pane skeleton - `app/(app)/inventory/loading.tsx` — table skeleton - `app/(app)/reports/loading.tsx` — chart skeleton - `app/(app)/flash-events/loading.tsx` — card-grid skeleton - `app/(app)/ai-design/loading.tsx` — hub skeleton - `app/(app)/marketing/loading.tsx` — card + stats skeleton - `app/(app)/consent-forms/loading.tsx` — table + tabs skeleton **Shared primitive** — `components/shared/PageSkeleton.tsx`: ```tsx export function PageSkeleton({ variant = 'list', }: { variant?: 'list' | 'grid' | 'two-pane' | 'tabs' | 'hub' }) { // returns a PageShell-wrapped skeleton matching the target page's structure // uses the existing primitive from components/ui/skeleton.tsx } ``` Each `loading.tsx` is a one-liner: ```tsx export default function Loading() { return } ``` **Impact:** User clicks → sees skeleton in <100 ms → perceived latency drops from 500 ms to instant. This is the single biggest UX win. --- ### Sprint B — Layout + server query perf (~60 min) **Goal:** Cut actual Server Component time by 200–300 ms per click. #### B1. Cache `getActiveStudio()` with React `cache()` File: `lib/context/active-studio.ts` Currently called from both `app/(app)/layout.tsx` AND from individual page files (payments, messages, inbox). Each call does 3 Supabase queries. Wrapping in React's `cache()` dedupes across a single request. ```ts import { cache } from 'react' export const getActiveStudio = cache(async function _getActiveStudio(): Promise { // existing impl }) ``` **Saving:** 50–100 ms on any page that calls `getActiveStudio()` after the layout already did. #### B2. Batch the multi-studio subscription query File: `lib/context/active-studio.ts` — currently N+1 (one subscription query per studio). Replace the `rows.map(async ...)` loop with one `.in('studio_id', [...])` call + map. **Saving:** 100–150 ms for users with 3+ studios (not most users, but eliminates a tail-latency bug). #### B3. Move layout badge queries behind Suspense File: `app/(app)/layout.tsx` Split the 8 badge-count queries out of the main layout render path: - Layout awaits ONLY the critical path: `getAuthenticatedUser` → `getActiveStudio` → `getActiveLocation` + profile. - Badge counts run inside a `` that's wrapped in `` — the sidebar renders immediately with badge=0, then streams the real counts in. **Saving:** ~150 ms — sidebar + page shell visible immediately, badges backfill. Alternative if Suspense refactor is too invasive: just wrap each badge count query in `unstable_cache()` with a 30-second TTL. Then most navigations hit the cache instead of re-querying. #### B4. Scope `/clients` SELECT to essential columns File: `app/(app)/clients/page.tsx` line 29. Drop 23 of the 35 selected columns (notes, address, pronouns, avatar_url, etc.) — the list view doesn't render them. Detail page keeps its own full select. **Saving:** 15–25 ms per clients-page load. #### B5. Limit + filter `inbox_assignments` query File: `app/(app)/inbox/page.tsx` Add `.or('archived_at.is.null,snoozed_until.gt.now()')` + `.limit(500)` to the assignments query. Currently pulls every archived assignment forever. **Saving:** 30–50 ms on studios with deep inbox history. #### B6. Dedup inbox unread-count query File: `app/(app)/inbox/page.tsx` — already fetched in the sidebar badge; no need to re-query inside the inbox page. **Saving:** 30–50 ms. #### B7. Add composite index for conversations inbox query New migration `supabase/migrations/20260424_conversations_unread_index.sql`: ```sql create index if not exists idx_conversations_studio_unread_active on conversations (studio_id, unread_count desc) where archived_at is null; ``` **Saving:** 20–40 ms per inbox load. --- ### Sprint C — Bundle trimming (~45 min) **Goal:** Smaller client JS = faster first paint, especially on Calendar. #### C1. Add `serverExternalPackages` to `next.config.ts` ```ts // next.config.ts const nextConfig: NextConfig = { // ... serverExternalPackages: ['twilio', '@sentry/nextjs', 'bullmq', 'ioredis', 'pdf-lib'], // ... } ``` Prevents server-only packages from leaking into the client bundle when pages import from `lib/` that transitively references them. **Saving:** ~500 KB off any route that transitively imports `lib/messaging/send.ts` or `lib/sms/twilio.ts`. #### C2. Add `optimizePackageImports` ```ts experimental: { optimizePackageImports: ['date-fns', 'lucide-react', '@tanstack/react-query'], }, ``` Next.js rewrites named imports to subpath imports automatically, dropping unused code. **Saving:** 30–50 KB. #### C3. Lazy-load FullCalendar File: `components/calendar/CalendarView.tsx` currently imports 5 FullCalendar modules at the top. Wrap the whole component in `dynamic(() => import('./CalendarViewInner'), { ssr: false })` with a skeleton fallback that matches the `loading.tsx` from Sprint A. **Saving:** 250 KB gzipped off the Calendar page's initial hydration. #### C4. Trim Inter font weights File: `app/layout.tsx` — currently loads 5 Inter weights (400, 500, 600, 700, 800). Grep the app and drop weights that aren't actually used (probably 500 and 800). **Saving:** 15–20 KB (2 fewer font files) + faster first paint. --- ### Sprint D — Polish (~30 min) #### D1. Prefetch hot sidebar links `components/app/sidebar/SidebarNavGroup.tsx` — Next.js already defaults to `prefetch=true` but add explicit `prefetch="intent"` on the top 5 routes (Dashboard, Inbox, Calendar, Clients, Projects) so the browser prioritizes them. #### D2. Memoize sidebar nav-groups computation File: `components/app/sidebar/AppSidebar.tsx` lines 62–74 — currently recomputes `navGroups` on every props change. Wrap in `useMemo` with `[role, permissions, locationCount]` deps so a dynamicBadges change doesn't trigger a full nav re-render. #### D3. Replace the 5 `` tags with `next/image` Grep finds 5 unoptimized images (mostly avatars + studio logos). Quick win for first paint + LQIP. #### D4. Route-specific React Query `staleTime` `lib/query-client.ts` has `staleTime: 60_000` globally. Override per-query: - Inbox / Appointments: 10 s (frequently changing) - Calendar: 5 s - Reports / Analytics: 120 s (heavy aggregates, tolerates stale) --- ## What this ships as **New files (2):** - `components/shared/PageSkeleton.tsx` - 15 `app/(app)/**/loading.tsx` files (each ~5 lines) - `supabase/migrations/20260424_conversations_unread_index.sql` **Modified files:** - `lib/context/active-studio.ts` (cache + batch subs) - `app/(app)/layout.tsx` (Suspense for badges) - `app/(app)/clients/page.tsx` (scoped select) - `app/(app)/inbox/page.tsx` (limit + dedup) - `next.config.ts` (serverExternalPackages + optimizePackageImports) - `components/calendar/CalendarView.tsx` (dynamic import) - `app/layout.tsx` (font weight trim) - `components/app/sidebar/SidebarNavGroup.tsx` (prefetch intent) - `components/app/sidebar/AppSidebar.tsx` (memoize navGroups) - `lib/query-client.ts` (route-specific staleTime) - 5 image files → `next/image` ## Expected end-state numbers | Fix | Perceived | Real | |---|---|---| | Sprint A: loading.tsx on 15 routes | **-400 to -700 ms per click** (feels instant) | 0 ms (same data time) | | Sprint B: cache + batch + Suspense + indexes + dedup | 0 ms (already skeleton-covered) | **-200 to -400 ms** | | Sprint C: bundle + serverExternalPackages + lazy Calendar | **-200 ms first paint, -500 KB transfer** | | | Sprint D: polish | **-50 ms** additional | | **Total: ~800–1200 ms of perceived latency cut per sidebar click.** Calendar page drops ~500 KB from its hydration bundle. Dev mode (`pnpm dev`) still slower than prod — those numbers assume production build. ## Out of scope - Migrating client-only pages back to Server Components (38 `'use client'` files under `app/`) — scope too broad, touch every feature, deferred to a dedicated refactor sprint - Splitting `globals.css` into per-route CSS modules — low ROI for this sprint - Sentry bundle trimming — needs bundle analyzer run first ## Verification - `pnpm typecheck` clean - `pnpm build` clean (note: local may fail on S19 WIP untracked files — CI will be clean) - Manual: login → click Dashboard → Inbox → Calendar → Clients → Projects → Messages. Each click shows skeleton within 100 ms, content arrives within 400 ms. - Lighthouse CI on `/dashboard` → LCP < 2.5 s, TBT < 300 ms - Bundle analyzer (`ANALYZE=true pnpm build`) → Calendar chunk < 200 KB (was >450 KB)

1	/**
2	 * Server-side helper to resolve the active studio context for the current user.
3	 *
4	 * Resolution order:
5	 *  1. Cookie `inkos_active_studio` (httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Max-Age 31536000)
6	 *  2. First membership ordered by studio_members.created_at ASC
7	 *
8	 * URL param `?studio=X` is honoured via <StudioParamSync> client component on mount —
9	 * it fires a POST to /api/context/set-studio which writes the cookie, then calls
10	 * router.refresh(). Layout reads only cookie + fallback (no search param in layout).
11	 *
12	 * Throws if the user has no studio memberships (caller redirects to /onboarding).
13	 */
14	
15	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
16	import { createClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server'
17	import type { Database } from '@/lib/supabase/types'
18	import type { PlanTier } from '@/lib/billing/feature-gate'
19	
20	export type StudioRow = Database['public']['Tables']['studios']['Row']
21	export type StudioMemberRow = Database['public']['Tables']['studio_members']['Row']
22	export type StudioMemberRole = StudioMemberRow['role']
23	
24	export interface StudioMembership {
25	  studioId: string
26	  studio: StudioRow
27	  role: StudioMemberRole
28	  /** Resolved subscription plan for this studio. Defaults 'solo' if no active sub. */
29	  plan: PlanTier
30	}
31	
32	export interface ActiveStudioContext {
33	  studioId: string
34	  studio: StudioRow
35	  role: StudioMemberRole
36	  plan: PlanTier
37	  allMemberships: StudioMembership[]
38	}
39	
40	export class NoStudioMembershipError extends Error {
41	  constructor() {
42	    super('User has no studio memberships')
43	    this.name = 'NoStudioMembershipError'
44	  }
45	}
46	
47	export async function getActiveStudio(): Promise<ActiveStudioContext> {
48	  const supabase = await createClient()
49	
50	  // 1. Identify current user
51	  const {
52	    data: { user },
53	    error: authError,
54	  } = await supabase.auth.getUser()
55	  if (authError || !user) {
56	    throw new NoStudioMembershipError()
57	  }
58	
59	  // 2. Fetch all memberships with studio data, ordered by created_at ASC
60	  const { data: rows, error: memberError } = await supabase
61	    .from('studio_members')
62	    .select(
63	      `
64	      studio_id,
65	      role,
66	      created_at,
67	      studios (
68	        id, name, slug, timezone, locale, currency, brand_color, logo_url, plan_id,
69	        custom_domain, custom_domain_verified, custom_domain_verified_at,
70	        white_label_enabled, custom_favicon_url, custom_email_from_name,
71	        custom_email_reply_to, powered_by_hidden, status, created_at, updated_at
72	      )
73	      `
74	    )
75	    .eq('user_id', user.id)
76	    .is('deactivated_at', null)
77	    .order('created_at', { ascending: true })
78	
79	  if (memberError || !rows || rows.length === 0) {
80	    throw new NoStudioMembershipError()
81	  }
82	
83	  // 3. Resolve plan for each studio (subscription lookup per studio_id)
84	  //    Use Promise.all with a small batch to avoid N+1 for users with many studios.
85	  const membershipsWithPlan: (StudioMembership | null)[] = await Promise.all(
86	    rows.map(async (row) => {
87	      // Type-safe studio extract — the join shape is deterministic
88	      const studio = (
89	        Array.isArray(row.studios) ? row.studios[0] : row.studios
90	      ) as StudioRow | null
91	
92	      if (!studio) {
93	        // Edge: studio row deleted but membership exists — skip gracefully
94	        return null
95	      }
96	
97	      let plan: PlanTier = 'solo'
98	      const { data: sub } = await supabase
99	        .from('subscriptions')
100	        .select('plan_tier')
101	        .eq('studio_id', row.studio_id)
102	        .eq('status', 'active')
103	        .maybeSingle()
104	      if (sub?.plan_tier) {
105	        plan = sub.plan_tier as PlanTier
106	      }
107	
108	      return {
109	        studioId: row.studio_id,
110	        studio,
111	        role: row.role as StudioMemberRole,
112	        plan,
113	      } satisfies StudioMembership
114	    })
115	  )
116	
117	  // Filter out any null slots (deleted studios)
118	  const validMemberships = membershipsWithPlan.filter(
119	    (m): m is StudioMembership => m !== null
120	  )
121	
122	  if (validMemberships.length === 0) {
123	    throw new NoStudioMembershipError()
124	  }
125	
126	  // 4. Resolve active studio from cookie
127	  const cookieStore = await cookies()
128	  const cookieValue = cookieStore.get('inkos_active_studio')?.value
129	
130	  let resolved: StudioMembership | undefined
131	
132	  if (cookieValue) {
133	    // Validate cookie value against actual memberships (defence-in-depth)
134	    resolved = validMemberships.find((m) => m.studioId === cookieValue)
135	    if (!resolved) {
136	      // Cookie holds a studio the user no longer belongs to — clear it
137	      // (Can't set cookies in layout Server Component; the route handler will clear it.
138	      //  Fall back silently here to the first membership.)
139	    }
140	  }
141	
142	  // 5. Fallback to first membership
143	  if (!resolved) {
144	    resolved = validMemberships[0]
145	  }
146	
147	  // validMemberships.length > 0 is guaranteed above (would have thrown otherwise)
148	  // resolved is now definitely defined
149	  const activeStudio = resolved as StudioMembership
150	
151	  return {
152	    studioId: activeStudio.studioId,
153	    studio: activeStudio.studio,
154	    role: activeStudio.role,
155	    plan: activeStudio.plan,
156	    allMemberships: validMemberships,
157	  }
158	}

const { studioId, role, plan } = activeStudio
  const sevenDaysAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString()
  const oneDayAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString()

  // Fetch all data sources in parallel
  const [
    pendingBookingsRes,
    consentSubmissionsRes,
    waitlistRes,
    newClientsRes,
    assignmentsRes,
    membersRes,
    unreadConversationsRes,
  ] = await Promise.all([
    // 1. Pending bookings — include scheduled_at for urgency
    supabase
      .from('bookings')
      .select('id, created_at, scheduled_at, clients(first_name, last_name)')
      .eq('studio_id', studioId)
      .eq('status', 'pending')
      .eq('deposit_paid', false)
      .order('scheduled_at', { ascending: true })
      .limit(50),

    // 2. Bookings with consent required but not yet signed (last 7d)
    supabase
      .from('bookings')
      .select('id, client_id, created_at, scheduled_at, clients(first_name, last_name)')
      .eq('studio_id', studioId)
      .eq('consent_required', true)
      .is('consent_signed_at', null)
      .gte('created_at', sevenDaysAgo)
      .order('scheduled_at', { ascending: true })
      .limit(30),

    // 3. Waitlist entries (last 24h)
    supabase
      .from('waitlist_entries')
      .select('id, client_id, created_at, clients(first_name, last_name)')
      .eq('studio_id', studioId)
      .eq('status', 'active')
      .gte('created_at', oneDayAgo)
      .order('created_at', { ascending: false })
      .limit(20),

    // 4. New clients (last 7d)
    supabase
      .from('clients')
      .select('id, first_name, last_name, created_at')
      .eq('studio_id', studioId)
      .gte('created_at', sevenDaysAgo)
      .is('archived_at', null)
      .order('created_at', { ascending: false })
      .limit(10),

    // 5. Inbox assignments (non-resolved, non-archived)
    supabase
      .from('inbox_assignments')
      .select('item_kind, item_id, assigned_to, snoozed_until, archived_at, resolved_at')
      .eq('studio_id', studioId),

    // 6. Studio members for assignment picker
    supabase
      .from('studio_members')
      .select('user_id, role, profiles(full_name, avatar_url)')
      .eq('studio_id', studioId)
      .is('deactivated_at', null),

    // 7. Unread message conversations
    supabase
      .from('conversations')
      .select('id, client_id, display_name, last_message_preview, last_message_at, unread_count, channel')
      .eq('studio_id', studioId)
      .is('archived_at', null)
      .gt('unread_count', 0)
      .order('last_message_at', { ascending: false })
      .limit(50),
  ])

1	/**
2	 * Server-side helper to resolve the active studio context for the current user.
3	 *
4	 * Resolution order:
5	 *  1. Cookie `inkos_active_studio` (httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Max-Age 31536000)
6	 *  2. First membership ordered by studio_members.created_at ASC
7	 *
8	 * URL param `?studio=X` is honoured via <StudioParamSync> client component on mount —
9	 * it fires a POST to /api/context/set-studio which writes the cookie, then calls
10	 * router.refresh(). Layout reads only cookie + fallback (no search param in layout).
11	 *
12	 * Throws if the user has no studio memberships (caller redirects to /onboarding).
13	 */
14	
15	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
16	import { createClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server'
17	import type { Database } from '@/lib/supabase/types'
18	import type { PlanTier } from '@/lib/billing/feature-gate'
19	
20	export type StudioRow = Database['public']['Tables']['studios']['Row']
21	export type StudioMemberRow = Database['public']['Tables']['studio_members']['Row']
22	export type StudioMemberRole = StudioMemberRow['role']
23	
24	export interface StudioMembership {
25	  studioId: string
26	  studio: StudioRow
27	  role: StudioMemberRole
28	  /** Resolved subscription plan for this studio. Defaults 'solo' if no active sub. */
29	  plan: PlanTier
30	}
31	
32	export interface ActiveStudioContext {
33	  studioId: string
34	  studio: StudioRow
35	  role: StudioMemberRole
36	  plan: PlanTier
37	  allMemberships: StudioMembership[]
38	}
39	
40	export class NoStudioMembershipError extends Error {
41	  constructor() {
42	    super('User has no studio memberships')
43	    this.name = 'NoStudioMembershipError'
44	  }
45	}
46	
47	export async function getActiveStudio(): Promise<ActiveStudioContext> {
48	  const supabase = await createClient()
49	
50	  // 1. Identify current user
51	  const {
52	    data: { user },
53	    error: authError,
54	  } = await supabase.auth.getUser()
55	  if (authError || !user) {
56	    throw new NoStudioMembershipError()
57	  }
58	
59	  // 2. Fetch all memberships with studio data, ordered by created_at ASC
60	  const { data: rows, error: memberError } = await supabase
61	    .from('studio_members')
62	    .select(
63	      `
64	      studio_id,
65	      role,
66	      created_at,
67	      studios (
68	        id, name, slug, timezone, locale, currency, brand_color, logo_url, plan_id,
69	        custom_domain, custom_domain_verified, custom_domain_verified_at,
70	        white_label_enabled, custom_favicon_url, custom_email_from_name,
71	        custom_email_reply_to, powered_by_hidden, status, created_at, updated_at
72	      )
73	      `
74	    )
75	    .eq('user_id', user.id)
76	    .is('deactivated_at', null)
77	    .order('created_at', { ascending: true })
78	
79	  if (memberError || !rows || rows.length === 0) {
80	    throw new NoStudioMembershipError()
81	  }
82	
83	  // 3. Resolve plan for each studio (subscription lookup per studio_id)
84	  //    Use Promise.all with a small batch to avoid N+1 for users with many studios.
85	  const membershipsWithPlan: (StudioMembership | null)[] = await Promise.all(
86	    rows.map(async (row) => {
87	      // Type-safe studio extract — the join shape is deterministic
88	      const studio = (
89	        Array.isArray(row.studios) ? row.studios[0] : row.studios
90	      ) as StudioRow | null
91	
92	      if (!studio) {
93	        // Edge: studio row deleted but membership exists — skip gracefully
94	        return null
95	      }
96	
97	      let plan: PlanTier = 'solo'
98	      const { data: sub } = await supabase
99	        .from('subscriptions')
100	        .select('plan_tier')
101	        .eq('studio_id', row.studio_id)
102	        .eq('status', 'active')
103	        .maybeSingle()
104	      if (sub?.plan_tier) {
105	        plan = sub.plan_tier as PlanTier
106	      }
107	
108	      return {
109	        studioId: row.studio_id,
110	        studio,
111	        role: row.role as StudioMemberRole,
112	        plan,
113	      } satisfies StudioMembership
114	    })
115	  )
116	
117	  // Filter out any null slots (deleted studios)
118	  const validMemberships = membershipsWithPlan.filter(
119	    (m): m is StudioMembership => m !== null
120	  )
121	
122	  if (validMemberships.length === 0) {
123	    throw new NoStudioMembershipError()
124	  }
125	
126	  // 4. Resolve active studio from cookie
127	  const cookieStore = await cookies()
128	  const cookieValue = cookieStore.get('inkos_active_studio')?.value
129	
130	  let resolved: StudioMembership | undefined
131	
132	  if (cookieValue) {
133	    // Validate cookie value against actual memberships (defence-in-depth)
134	    resolved = validMemberships.find((m) => m.studioId === cookieValue)

1	import { QueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'
2	
3	/**
4	 * Creates a new QueryClient with production-ready defaults.
5	 *
6	 * Used in QueryProvider to create per-request client on the server
7	 * and a singleton client on the browser.
8	 */
9	export function makeQueryClient(): QueryClient {
10	  return new QueryClient({
11	    defaultOptions: {
12	      queries: {
13	        // Data is considered fresh for 60 seconds by default
14	        staleTime: 60_000,
15	        // Retry once on failure (default 3 is too aggressive)
16	        retry: 1,
17	        // Don't refetch on window focus in dev (annoying)
18	        refetchOnWindowFocus: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production',
19	      },
20	      mutations: {
21	        retry: 0,
22	      },
23	    },
24	  })
25	}
26	
27	let browserQueryClient: QueryClient | undefined
28	
29	/**
30	 * Returns the singleton QueryClient for browser usage.
31	 * Creates it on first call. Safe to call in Client Components.
32	 */
33	export function getQueryClient(): QueryClient {
34	  if (typeof window === 'undefined') {
35	    // Server: always make a new client (prevents cross-request state sharing)
36	    return makeQueryClient()
37	  }
38	  // Browser: reuse the same client across renders
39	  browserQueryClient ??= makeQueryClient()
40	  return browserQueryClient
41	}

Responsive typography on mobile (perceived polish, especially at 375px) **Complexity level:** Medium. # InkOS — Login page deep redesign

## Context

User wants the `/login` page re-engineered to production-grade: brand-forward, conversion-optimized, and tailored for tattoo studio owners + artists (not generic SaaS).

**Current state (from Explore audit):**
- Split-screen layout already matches Brand Book v1.0 (Bone / Onyx / Stone / Rust), shared with `/signup` and `/forgot-password` via `app/(auth)/layout.tsx`
- Auth is wired: email+password, Google OAuth, password reset (magic-link email)
- Foundation is solid — gaps are in friction (no show/hide password), mobile order (Google buried below email), copy (generic SaaS bullets, not tattoo-specific), and visible trust signals

**Goal:** keep what works, cut friction, sharpen the copy for the audience, raise conversion.

## Design direction (locked by Brand Book v1.0)

| Token | Use |
|---|---|
| **Bone** `#F7F7F5` | Right panel background + card surface |
| **Onyx** `#0F0F0F` | Left panel + primary text + primary CTA |
| **Stone** `#787774` | Secondary text, labels, borders |
| **Rust** `#B23A2B` | Accent italics (hero) + active/error states ONLY |
| Inter | Form labels, inputs, buttons, body |
| Instrument Serif | Left-panel hero + italic accent words |
| JetBrains Mono | Never on auth |
| radius-2xl | Card |
| radius-lg | Inputs / buttons |
| shadow-soft-md | Card elevation |

No new tokens. No new fonts. Discipline is the brand.

## Redesign — 5 concrete improvements

### 1. Create `<PasswordInput>` primitive (shared across login, signup, reset)

New file: `components/ui/password-input.tsx`

```tsx
interface PasswordInputProps extends Omit<InputProps, 'type'> { /* rest */ }
// Wraps <Input type={show ? 'text' : 'password'} />
// Right-side Eye/EyeOff button inside the input, 28px touch target
// Keyboard accessible: Tab to toggle, aria-pressed, aria-label switches between "Show password" / "Hide password"
// No visible background; only a subtle Stone icon tint, Rust on focus
```

Immediately adopted by `LoginForm`, `SignupForm`, and `ResetPasswordForm`. Removes the biggest mobile friction (predictive text typo, can't verify).

### 2. LoginForm rework (`components/auth/LoginForm.tsx`)

Full structural rewrite. Final shape (top to bottom):

```
[Heading] "Welcome back"
[Subheading] "Sign in to your studio"

[Google button]                              ← moved to top (mobile-first)
  "Continue with Google"
  Full-width, Onyx outline, 40px height

[Divider]  or continue with email

[Email field]
  Label: "Email"   (lowercase, Stone)
  Input with inline error below

[Password field]
  Label: "Password"     Forgot password? →  (right-aligned link)
  <PasswordInput>       with eye toggle
  Inline error below

[Primary CTA — Onyx fill]
  "Sign in" (idle)  →  spinner + "Signing in…" (loading)
  Full width, 44px height on mobile for a fat touch target

[Magic-link alt — subtle link]                ← new
  "Email me a sign-in link instead"
  Text link, Stone color, small
  Only shown after the first failed login OR always-visible below CTA

[Footer row]
  "New to InkOS? → Start free trial"          ← action-oriented, not "Sign up"
```

Behavior + polish:
- Loading state: button shows `<Loader2 className="animate-spin" />` + updated label (NOT just text change)
- Error state: inline under field, red/Rust color, `role="alert"`, preserved on re-type (clears on input)
- Rate-limit / locked-out: non-destructive toast if 5+ attempts, suggests password reset
- Post-login: keep existing redirect logic (`/dashboard` unless `?redirectedFrom`)
- Google flow: button shows spinner while the redirect is negotiating
- Magic link flow (new): wires `supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ email })` then swaps the form for a confirmation screen ("Check your inbox at yash@boldteq.com") with a "Send again" secondary action and 60-second cooldown

### 3. Left-panel rewrite (`app/(auth)/layout.tsx`)

**Current:**
```
The studio, run with restraint.
• Bookings, schedule & waitlist in one view
• Client CRM with full session history
• Commissions, payroll & billing — automated
```

**New:**
```
The studio, run with restraint.
No chaos. No spreadsheets. No per-seat fees.

[icon · Calendar]    All-artist calendar, one view
                     Guest spots, waitlist, deposits — in the same week.

[icon · Users]       One CRM. Every session, every note.
                     Client history, consent forms, referrals — automated.

[icon · DollarSign]  Commissions, payroll, 1099s — done.
                     Flat fee. Unlimited artists. No surprises at payout.
```

Each bullet has a 24px Onyx icon chip + 13px Inter title (700) + 12px Stone description.

**Footer band** (replace the generic "FOUR COLORS · TWO TYPEFACES · ONE VOICE"):

```
BUILT BY INKERS, FOR INKERS
```

+ below that, a thin row of grayscale studio-logo placeholders OR (if no real logos) a single muted line: "Used by studios in 12 countries." Only include if the claim is provable — otherwise the "Built by inkers, for inkers" line stands alone. (User should confirm which.)

**Mobile scale** — add responsive type scale so the hero doesn't overflow on 375px:
```
hero: text-3xl sm:text-4xl lg:text-5xl
body: text-sm sm:text-base
```

### 4. Signup + ForgotPassword alignment

`components/auth/SignupForm.tsx`:
- Adopt the same `<PasswordInput>` with show/hide
- Mirror the Google-first order on mobile
- Heading: "Start your studio" (action-oriented, not "Create account")
- Sub: "Free for 14 days. No card required."
- Final CTA: "Start free trial →"
- Keep the existing `<PasswordStrengthBar />` below the password field

`components/auth/ForgotPasswordForm.tsx`:
- Heading: "Reset your password"
- Sub: "We'll email you a secure link."
- Single field (Email) + "Send reset link"
- After submit: same in-place confirmation screen pattern as magic link
- "Remembered your password? → Sign in"

Both pages get a consistent voice.

### 5. Trust + compliance footnote

Tiny text below the form card (Stone, 11px):

```
Secured by Supabase Auth · GDPR + HIPAA-aware · SOC 2 roadmap Q4 2026
```

Only include claims that are true today (Supabase Auth is true; GDPR-aware is true if we've done the basics; drop anything we can't defend).

## Mobile (375–768 px) specifics

- Left panel `hidden lg:flex` — already correct
- Card width: `w-full max-w-[420px]` — keep
- Padding: `p-5 sm:p-6 lg:p-10` — tighter on mobile
- Form spacing: `space-y-4 sm:space-y-5`
- CTA touch targets: 44px min on mobile, 40px on desktop
- Google button reorders to top on mobile via flex-col ordering, NOT via CSS `order:` (for semantic correctness in serial reader flow)
- Keyboard-aware bottom padding already handled by existing `useKeyboardAware` hook — do not touch

## Accessibility

- Every input gets an explicit `<Label htmlFor>`, no placeholder-as-label
- Errors use `role="alert"` + `aria-invalid="true"` on the input
- Password show/hide button: `aria-pressed`, `aria-label` that reads "Show password" / "Hide password"
- Focus trap inside the card (native, no override)
- Logical tab order: Email → Password → Show/Hide → Forgot → CTA → Google → Sign up link
- Color contrast: Stone text on Bone = 4.6:1 (passes AA), Onyx on Bone = 17:1

## Files

**Create (1):**
- `components/ui/password-input.tsx`

**Modify (4):**
- `components/auth/LoginForm.tsx` — full rewrite using new primitive, reorder, magic link, loading polish
- `components/auth/SignupForm.tsx` — adopt PasswordInput, mirror Google-first order, new copy
- `components/auth/ForgotPasswordForm.tsx` — consistent voice + confirmation-screen pattern
- `app/(auth)/layout.tsx` — hero rewrite, new feature bullets, footer tagline, mobile type scale

**No changes:**
- Supabase client, server, middleware — auth flows are correct
- `app/globals.css` — tokens already in place

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck` clean
- `pnpm build` clean
- Manual: `/login`, `/signup`, `/forgot-password` all render in light AND dark Brand Book modes (note: auth pages stay Bone/Onyx; dark-mode toggle lives only inside the authed app)
- Mobile 375px: all three pages render without overflow, CTAs reachable above the keyboard
- Password toggle: clicking Eye shows text; aria state correct; no flash of plaintext on autofill
- Google button spinner appears during OAuth redirect
- Magic-link email arrives within 30 seconds; confirmation screen shows cooldown + "send again"

## Out of scope

- Passkeys / WebAuthn (needs Supabase Auth update + device capability UX) — S20+
- Apple OAuth (needs Apple Developer account setup) — S20+
- Landing-page-style scroll sections on `/login` (would dilute focus) — not this sprint
- A/B test instrumentation — not this sprint; ship the redesign and measure with the existing analytics

# InkOS — Login page deep redesign

## Context

User wants the `/login` page re-engineered to production-grade: brand-forward, conversion-optimized, and tailored for tattoo studio owners + artists (not generic SaaS).

**Current state (from Explore audit):**
- Split-screen layout already matches Brand Book v1.0 (Bone / Onyx / Stone / Rust), shared with `/signup` and `/forgot-password` via `app/(auth)/layout.tsx`
- Auth is wired: email+password, Google OAuth, password reset (magic-link email)
- Foundation is solid — gaps are in friction (no show/hide password), mobile order (Google buried below email), copy (generic SaaS bullets, not tattoo-specific), and visible trust signals

**Goal:** keep what works, cut friction, sharpen the copy for the audience, raise conversion.

## Design direction (locked by Brand Book v1.0)

| Token | Use |
|---|---|
| **Bone** `#F7F7F5` | Right panel background + card surface |
| **Onyx** `#0F0F0F` | Left panel + primary text + primary CTA |
| **Stone** `#787774` | Secondary text, labels, borders |
| **Rust** `#B23A2B` | Accent italics (hero) + active/error states ONLY |
| Inter | Form labels, inputs, buttons, body |
| Instrument Serif | Left-panel hero + italic accent words |
| JetBrains Mono | Never on auth |
| radius-2xl | Card |
| radius-lg | Inputs / buttons |
| shadow-soft-md | Card elevation |

No new tokens. No new fonts. Discipline is the brand.

## Redesign — 5 concrete improvements

### 1. Create `<PasswordInput>` primitive (shared across login, signup, reset)

New file: `components/ui/password-input.tsx`

```tsx
interface PasswordInputProps extends Omit<InputProps, 'type'> { /* rest */ }
// Wraps <Input type={show ? 'text' : 'password'} />
// Right-side Eye/EyeOff button inside the input, 28px touch target
// Keyboard accessible: Tab to toggle, aria-pressed, aria-label switches between "Show password" / "Hide password"
// No visible background; only a subtle Stone icon tint, Rust on focus
```

Immediately adopted by `LoginForm`, `SignupForm`, and `ResetPasswordForm`. Removes the biggest mobile friction (predictive text typo, can't verify).

### 2. LoginForm rework (`components/auth/LoginForm.tsx`)

Full structural rewrite. Final shape (top to bottom):

```
[Heading] "Welcome back"
[Subheading] "Sign in to your studio"

[Google button]                              ← moved to top (mobile-first)
  "Continue with Google"
  Full-width, Onyx outline, 40px height

[Divider]  or continue with email

[Email field]
  Label: "Email"   (lowercase, Stone)
  Input with inline error below

[Password field]
  Label: "Password"     Forgot password? →  (right-aligned link)
  <PasswordInput>       with eye toggle
  Inline error below

[Primary CTA — Onyx fill]
  "Sign in" (idle)  →  spinner + "Signing in…" (loading)
  Full width, 44px height on mobile for a fat touch target

[Magic-link alt — subtle link]                ← new
  "Email me a sign-in link instead"
  Text link, Stone color, small
  Only shown after the first failed login OR always-visible below CTA

[Footer row]
  "New to InkOS? → Start free trial"          ← action-oriented, not "Sign up"
```

Behavior + polish:
- Loading state: button shows `<Loader2 className="animate-spin" />` + updated label (NOT just text change)
- Error state: inline under field, red/Rust color, `role="alert"`, preserved on re-type (clears on input)
- Rate-limit / locked-out: non-destructive toast if 5+ attempts, suggests password reset
- Post-login: keep existing redirect logic (`/dashboard` unless `?redirectedFrom`)
- Google flow: button shows spinner while the redirect is negotiating
- Magic link flow (new): wires `supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ email })` then swaps the form for a confirmation screen ("Check your inbox at yash@boldteq.com") with a "Send again" secondary action and 60-second cooldown

### 3. Left-panel rewrite (`app/(auth)/layout.tsx`)

**Current:**
```
The studio, run with restraint.
• Bookings, schedule & waitlist in one view
• Client CRM with full session history
• Commissions, payroll & billing — automated
```

**New:**
```
The studio, run with restraint.
No chaos. No spreadsheets. No per-seat fees.

[icon · Calendar]    All-artist calendar, one view
                     Guest spots, waitlist, deposits — in the same week.

[icon · Users]       One CRM. Every session, every note.
                     Client history, consent forms, referrals — automated.

[icon · DollarSign]  Commissions, payroll, 1099s — done.
                     Flat fee. Unlimited artists. No surprises at payout.
```

Each bullet has a 24px Onyx icon chip + 13px Inter title (700) + 12px Stone description.

**Footer band** (replace the generic "FOUR COLORS · TWO TYPEFACES · ONE VOICE"):

```
BUILT BY INKERS, FOR INKERS
```

+ below that, a thin row of grayscale studio-logo placeholders OR (if no real logos) a single muted line: "Used by studios in 12 countries." Only include if the claim is provable — otherwise the "Built by inkers, for inkers" line stands alone. (User should confirm which.)

**Mobile scale** — add responsive type scale so the hero doesn't overflow on 375px:
```
hero: text-3xl sm:text-4xl lg:text-5xl
body: text-sm sm:text-base
```

### 4. Signup + ForgotPassword alignment

`components/auth/SignupForm.tsx`:
- Adopt the same `<PasswordInput>` with show/hide
- Mirror the Google-first order on mobile
- Heading: "Start your studio" (action-oriented, not "Create account")
- Sub: "Free for 14 days. No card required."
- Final CTA: "Start free trial →"
- Keep the existing `<PasswordStrengthBar />` below the password field

`components/auth/ForgotPasswordForm.tsx`:
- Heading: "Reset your password"
- Sub: "We'll email you a secure link."
- Single field (Email) + "Send reset link"
- After submit: same in-place confirmation screen pattern as magic link
- "Remembered your password? → Sign in"

Both pages get a consistent voice.

### 5. Trust + compliance footnote

Tiny text below the form card (Stone, 11px):

```
Secured by Supabase Auth · GDPR + HIPAA-aware · SOC 2 roadmap Q4 2026
```

Only include claims that are true today (Supabase Auth is true; GDPR-aware is true if we've done the basics; drop anything we can't defend).

## Mobile (375–768 px) specifics

- Left panel `hidden lg:flex` — already correct
- Card width: `w-full max-w-[420px]` — keep
- Padding: `p-5 sm:p-6 lg:p-10` — tighter on mobile
- Form spacing: `space-y-4 sm:space-y-5`
- CTA touch targets: 44px min on mobile, 40px on desktop
- Google button reorders to top on mobile via flex-col ordering, NOT via CSS `order:` (for semantic correctness in serial reader flow)
- Keyboard-aware bottom padding already handled by existing `useKeyboardAware` hook — do not touch

## Accessibility

- Every input gets an explicit `<Label htmlFor>`, no placeholder-as-label
- Errors use `role="alert"` + `aria-invalid="true"` on the input
- Password show/hide button: `aria-pressed`, `aria-label` that reads "Show password" / "Hide password"
- Focus trap inside the card (native, no override)
- Logical tab order: Email → Password → Show/Hide → Forgot → CTA → Google → Sign up link
- Color contrast: Stone text on Bone = 4.6:1 (passes AA), Onyx on Bone = 17:1

## Files

**Create (1):**
- `components/ui/password-input.tsx`

**Modify (4):**
- `components/auth/LoginForm.tsx` — full rewrite using new primitive, reorder, magic link, loading polish
- `components/auth/SignupForm.tsx` — adopt PasswordInput, mirror Google-first order, new copy
- `components/auth/ForgotPasswordForm.tsx` — consistent voice + confirmation-screen pattern
- `app/(auth)/layout.tsx` — hero rewrite, new feature bullets, footer tagline, mobile type scale

**No changes:**
- Supabase client, server, middleware — auth flows are correct
- `app/globals.css` — tokens already in place

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck` clean
- `pnpm build` clean
- Manual: `/login`, `/signup`, `/forgot-password` all render in light AND dark Brand Book modes (note: auth pages stay Bone/Onyx; dark-mode toggle lives only inside the authed app)
- Mobile 375px: all three pages render without overflow, CTAs reachable above the keyboard
- Password toggle: clicking Eye shows text; aria state correct; no flash of plaintext on autofill
- Google button spinner appears during OAuth redirect
- Magic-link email arrives within 30 seconds; confirmation screen shows cooldown + "send again"

## Out of scope

- Passkeys / WebAuthn (needs Supabase Auth update + device capability UX) — S20+
- Apple OAuth (needs Apple Developer account setup) — S20+
- Landing-page-style scroll sections on `/login` (would dilute focus) — not this sprint

Now I have all the information I need. Let me create the audit report:

## AUDIT: Clients Page Top-Bar Implementation — InkOS Next.js 16

### FILE INVENTORY & RENDERING STRUCTURE

**Server-side (page.tsx):**
- `/app/(app)/clients/page.tsx` — RSC that renders `PageShell` > `PageHeader` > `ClientsPageClient` (Suspense-wrapped)

**Client-side (ClientsPageClient.tsx):**
- `/app/(app)/clients/ClientsPageClient.tsx` — 520 lines; orchestrates all top-bar state and child component props

**The top-bar is rendered across THREE zones** (not unified):

1. **Zone 1 (Rows 293–340):** `PageViews` wrapper + `SavedViewSwitcher` + right-aligned count/inactive-badge/CTA
2. **Zone 2 (Lines 343–375):** Unsaved changes banner (conditional)
3. **Zone 3 (Lines 377–381):** `ClientFilterBar` — search + filter popovers + toggle buttons

**Shared Primitives Used:**
- `PageHeader` (title + description at top) 
- `PageShell` (page container w/ padding rhythm)
- `PageViews` (view picker zone — left flex + right actions slot)
- `PageTabs` (exists but not used for clients; used in /appointments, /payments)
- `SavedViewSwitcher` (pill-based view selector, not tabs)

---

### CURRENT JSX STRUCTURE (Condensed Pseudo-Code)

```
<PageShell>
  <PageHeader title="Clients" description="..." />
  
  <PullToRefresh>
    {/* Zone 1: View tabs + count/inactive badge + New button */}
    <PageViews bordered actions={<count/inactive/button>}>
      <SavedViewSwitcher 
        views={...} 
        activeViewId={...}
        onViewChange={handleViewChange}
        onCreateView={...}
        onEditView={...}
        onDuplicateView={...}
        onDeleteView={...}
        onSetDefault={...}
      />
    </PageViews>
    
    {/* Zone 2: Unsaved changes banner (conditional) */}
    {hasUnsavedChanges && activeView && !activeView.is_system && (
      <Alert>Unsaved changes...</Alert>
    )}
    
    {/* Zone 3: Search + filter bar */}
    <ClientFilterBar
      filters={...}
      onChange={handleFiltersChange}
      tagLibrary={...}
    />
    
    {/* Zone 4: Bulk action bar (conditional, only when rows selected) */}
    {selectedIds.length > 0 && (
      <BulkActionsBar {...} />
    )}
    
    {/* Zone 5: Table + states */}
    <DataState><ClientsTable /></DataState>
  </PullToRefresh>
</PageShell>
```

**Total top-bar height on desktop:** ~48px (PageHeader: 36px serif title + 16px description + gaps) + 40px (PageViews row) + 36px (FilterBar row, single line) + optional banner/bulk-action = **140–180px** depending on state.

---

### EXISTING PRIMITIVES: WHAT YOU CAN REUSE

| Primitive | Location | Current Use | API Notes |
|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------|
| `PageHeader` | `components/shared/PageHeader.tsx` | Clients/Appointments/Payments title+desc | `title`, `description`, `actions`, `breadcrumb`, `backHref`; renders serif font + rust hairline |
| `PageShell` | `components/shared/PageShell.tsx` | Wraps all pages | `fullHeight` (opt), `maxWidth`, `innerClassName`; handles page bg + radial gradients + 24px rhythm |
| `PageViews` | `components/shared/PageViews.tsx` | View picker zone | `children` (left), `actions` (right), `bordered` (adds bottom hairline); flex + mobile scroll/fade-mask |
| `PageTabs` | `components/shared/PageTabs.tsx` | /appointments, /payments (tab rows) | `tabs[]`, `activeKey`, `currentPlan`, `currentRole`; URL persistence via `?tab=`; plan gating; keyboard nav |
| `SavedViewSwitcher` | `components/clients/SavedViewSwitcher.tsx` | Clients only (view pills) | Pills w/ dropdown on active; `New view` button; star for default; context menu (edit/dup/delete/set-default) |

**What's missing:**
- No unified "column picker" component (button exists in FilterBar but no modal/popover wired)
- No "Columns" menu implementation (placeholder button only)
- No consolidated top-bar toolbar component (zone 1 + 3 are separate elements)

---

# InkOS — Login page deep redesign

## Context

User wants the `/login` page re-engineered to production-grade: brand-forward, conversion-optimized, and tailored for tattoo studio owners + artists (not generic SaaS).

**Current state (from Explore audit):**
- Split-screen layout already matches Brand Book v1.0 (Bone / Onyx / Stone / Rust), shared with `/signup` and `/forgot-password` via `app/(auth)/layout.tsx`
- Auth is wired: email+password, Google OAuth, password reset (magic-link email)
- Foundation is solid — gaps are in friction (no show/hide password), mobile order (Google buried below email), copy (generic SaaS bullets, not tattoo-specific), and visible trust signals

**Goal:** keep what works, cut friction, sharpen the copy for the audience, raise conversion.

## Design direction (locked by Brand Book v1.0)

| Token | Use |
|---|---|
| **Bone** `#F7F7F5` | Right panel background + card surface |
| **Onyx** `#0F0F0F` | Left panel + primary text + primary CTA |
| **Stone** `#787774` | Secondary text, labels, borders |
| **Rust** `#B23A2B` | Accent italics (hero) + active/error states ONLY |
| Inter | Form labels, inputs, buttons, body |
| Instrument Serif | Left-panel hero + italic accent words |
| JetBrains Mono | Never on auth |
| radius-2xl | Card |
| radius-lg | Inputs / buttons |
| shadow-soft-md | Card elevation |

No new tokens. No new fonts. Discipline is the brand.

## Redesign — 5 concrete improvements

### 1. Create `<PasswordInput>` primitive (shared across login, signup, reset)

New file: `components/ui/password-input.tsx`

```tsx
interface PasswordInputProps extends Omit<InputProps, 'type'> { /* rest */ }
// Wraps <Input type={show ? 'text' : 'password'} />
// Right-side Eye/EyeOff button inside the input, 28px touch target
// Keyboard accessible: Tab to toggle, aria-pressed, aria-label switches between "Show password" / "Hide password"
// No visible background; only a subtle Stone icon tint, Rust on focus
```

Immediately adopted by `LoginForm`, `SignupForm`, and `ResetPasswordForm`. Removes the biggest mobile friction (predictive text typo, can't verify).

### 2. LoginForm rework (`components/auth/LoginForm.tsx`)

Full structural rewrite. Final shape (top to bottom):

```
[Heading] "Welcome back"
[Subheading] "Sign in to your studio"

[Google button]                              ← moved to top (mobile-first)
  "Continue with Google"
  Full-width, Onyx outline, 40px height

[Divider]  or continue with email

[Email field]
  Label: "Email"   (lowercase, Stone)
  Input with inline error below

[Password field]
  Label: "Password"     Forgot password? →  (right-aligned link)
  <PasswordInput>       with eye toggle
  Inline error below

[Primary CTA — Onyx fill]
  "Sign in" (idle)  →  spinner + "Signing in…" (loading)
  Full width, 44px height on mobile for a fat touch target

[Magic-link alt — subtle link]                ← new
  "Email me a sign-in link instead"
  Text link, Stone color, small
  Only shown after the first failed login OR always-visible below CTA

[Footer row]
  "New to InkOS? → Start free trial"          ← action-oriented, not "Sign up"
```

Behavior + polish:
- Loading state: button shows `<Loader2 className="animate-spin" />` + updated label (NOT just text change)
- Error state: inline under field, red/Rust color, `role="alert"`, preserved on re-type (clears on input)
- Rate-limit / locked-out: non-destructive toast if 5+ attempts, suggests password reset

---MIGRATION CONTENT---
-- ============================================================
-- S23a: clients.pronouns + clients.avatar_url + client-avatars storage bucket
-- Supports the Clients Page Audit v1: add pronouns field, avatar upload,
-- and the private bucket to host per-client profile photos.
-- Allergies intentionally NOT added as a column — they live in
-- client_notes (category='allergies', is_pinned=true) and are surfaced
-- via the existing client_health_summary view + HealthAlertBadge.
-- ============================================================

-- ── 1. Add columns to clients ────────────────────────────────
alter table public.clients
  add column if not exists pronouns text,
  add column if not exists avatar_url text;

comment on column public.clients.pronouns is
  'Free-text pronouns (he/him, she/her, they/them, or custom). Nullable.';
comment on column public.clients.avatar_url is
  'Signed URL or public path to the client profile photo. Stored in client-avatars bucket.';

-- ── 2. client-avatars storage bucket (PRIVATE) ───────────────
-- Avatars are personally identifiable so the bucket is NOT public.
-- Reads are served via signed URLs generated in the API layer.
-- Path: {studio_id}/{client_id}/{filename}
insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types)
values (
  'client-avatars',
  'client-avatars',
  false,
  5242880, -- 5MB
  array['image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/webp']
)
on conflict (id) do nothing;

-- ── 3. RLS for client-avatars bucket ─────────────────────────

-- SELECT: any member of the studio whose id is the first path segment
create policy "client_avatars_storage_select"
  on storage.objects for select
  using (
    bucket_id = 'client-avatars'
    and exists (
      select 1 from public.studio_members sm
      where sm.studio_id::text = (storage.foldername(name))[1]
        and sm.user_id = auth.uid()
        and sm.deactivated_at is null
    )
  );

-- INSERT: owner / admin / artist / receptionist of the studio
create policy "client_avatars_storage_insert"

**Root cause identified + catchup script shipped.**

## What's happening

`/clients` throws `Failed to fetch clients` because the API's SELECT includes columns (`is_banned`, `banned_reason`, `banned_at`, `banned_by`, `pronouns`, `avatar_url`) that only exist once the **S18a** and **S23a** migrations have run on prod Supabase. Prod is still on the old schema baseline — same drift pattern as the earlier S18 catchup.

## Fix (PR #13 merged to main)

`scripts/s19-prod-catchup.sql` bundles the **15 migrations** that landed after the S18 catchup was run:

```
20260423 — helper_set_updated_at, s18a_client_social_ban (← fixes the 500), s18b_health_summary_view
20260424 — s19a_booking_participants, s19c_artist_goals + performance_view,
           s19d_studio_custom_roles + seed_default_permissions
20260425 — s20a_flash_event_assets_bucket, s20c_artist_portfolio_items, s20d_style_tags
20260426 — s21a_studio_intake_policy, s21b_template_note_mapping
20260427 — s22_user_pinned_items
20260428 — s23a_clients_pronouns_avatar (← fixes the 500)
```

## What you do

1. Supabase dashboard → SQL editor (prod project)
2. Paste `scripts/s19-prod-catchup.sql` → Run (safe to re-run; idempotent)
3. Run the 4 sanity queries at the bottom — expect 6 new client columns, 7 new tables, 2 new views, 1 helper function
4. Verify 3 storage buckets exist (`client-avatars`, `flash-event-assets`, `artist-portfolio`) in Storage tab — usually auto-created but confirm

After that, hard-refresh `/clients` in incognito — the table should render and the toast is gone. Every other page that touches the newer schema (booking participants, artist goals, leaderboard, portfolio, style tags, pinned items) will come back online at the same time.

This is becoming a recurring pattern. Two options to stop it going forward: (a) wire Supabase CLI migration auto-apply to Railway CI so prod stays in sync, or (b) strip the not-yet-deployed columns out of the SELECTs until the migrations land. Worth a small ops sprint soon.
